title: Liang Dynasty
capsule: The Liang dynasty (梁朝, 502-557), third of China's Southern Dynasties, was founded when Xiao Yan deposed the Southern Qi and took the throne as Emperor Wu, a devout Buddhist patron whose 47-year reign became one of the most stable and culturally flourishing of the era. That stability collapsed after 548, when the renegade general Hou Jing rebelled, sacked the capital Jiankang, and effectively imprisoned Emperor Wu, who died in 549; his sons Emperor Jianwen and Emperor Yuan struggled to restore order amid civil war before the general Chen Baxian deposed the last Liang emperor, Emperor Jing, in 557 and founded the Chen dynasty. A rump Liang state, the Western Liang, survived as a Western Wei/Northern Zhou client at Jiangling into the 580s.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution.
